name: Co-ops of Whatcom County — when
note: Timeline companion to the graph 'Co-ops of Whatcom County' (RCN Map issue whatcom-wa--cooperatives). One bar per co-op from founding to today; grey bars are the firms that came before a conversion; gold, green and purple bars are the dated ties (money, trade, co-op development) from the graph. Year-only dates sit at mid-year with half a year of fuzz. Undated ties carry wide fuzz and low confidence rather than invented precision. Cascade Cooperatives memberships (13) and the NWCDC support for Circle of Life are not drawn: no dates are published. Researched Sep 2026 by Marc Pierson with Claude Opus 5.5.

intervals.label: WECU (Whatcom Educational CU)
intervals.note: Founded 1936. Year only. Not a Cascade Cooperatives member.

intervals.label: North Coast Credit Union
intervals.note: Founded 1939. Year only. Cascade Cooperatives member.

intervals.label: Industrial Credit Union
intervals.note: Founded 1941. Year only. Cascade Cooperatives member.

intervals.label: ICU absorbs Ferndale Refinery CU
intervals.note: Merger effective Oct 1 2012.

intervals.label: WestEdge Credit Union
intervals.note: Founded 1953. Year only. Cascade Cooperatives member.

intervals.label: Community Food Co-op
intervals.note: Opened 1970 in Fairhaven with one storefront. Cascade Cooperatives member.

intervals.label: Food Co-op Farm Fund
intervals.note: Since 2000: over $878,000 to 164 local food and farm projects.

intervals.label: Farm Fund loan fund (with ICU)
intervals.note: Full title: Farm Fund secured loan fund (with ICU and Whatcom Community Foundation). Start date not published. Listed among the Farm Fund's pre-2016 projects and described as on its 'third round of circulation', so it began well before 2016. Start fuzz is wide on purpose.

intervals.label: REI Bellingham store
intervals.note: REI is a national consumer co-op (1938); the Bellingham store opened 1999.

intervals.label: A-1 Builders (conventional firm)
intervals.note: A-1 Builders from 1955 (roots as Washington Builders, 1928). Owned by Rick Dubrow from 1976.

intervals.label: A1DesignBuild — worker co-op
intervals.note: Converted to a worker co-op in 2017 with five worker-owners. Cascade Cooperatives member.

intervals.label: Bellingham Bay Builders
intervals.note: Worker co-op founded 2004. Cascade Cooperatives member.

intervals.label: Circle of Life Caregiver Cooperative
intervals.note: Opened 2009 — the oldest home-care co-op in Washington. NWCDC lists it among the home-care co-ops it serves; when that support began is not published, so it is not linked.

intervals.label: Yellow Cab of Whatcom-Skagit (conventional firm)
intervals.note: Founded 1992 by Ron Wielenga of Lynden.

intervals.label: Yellow Cab Co-op — worker-owned
intervals.note: Employee-owned since August 2023. Cascade Cooperatives member.

intervals.label: Cascade Mountain Ascents
intervals.note: Worker-owned guiding collective, founded 2023. Cascade Cooperatives member.

intervals.label: Community Media Cooperative
intervals.note: Worker co-op established 2023. Cascade Cooperatives member.

intervals.label: Cooperativa Tierra y Libertad
intervals.who: Cascade Cooperatives co-op map (2026); PCC Sound Consumer 2023
intervals.note: Washington's first farmworker-owned co-op farm, launched 2017 on 65 acres near Everson.

intervals.label: Tierra y Libertad produce sold at the Food Co-op
intervals.note: The June 2023 article lists the Bellingham food co-op among Tierra y Libertad's buyers. When sales began is not published; placed after the 2017 launch with wide fuzz.

intervals.label: Cascadia Deaf Nation
intervals.note: Social co-op founded 2016. Cascade Cooperatives member.

intervals.label: United Dairymen's Association → Darigold (Lynden plant)
intervals.note: Darigold's predecessor, the United Dairymen's Association, was founded in Lynden in summer 1918. Not a Cascade Cooperatives member.

intervals.label: Whatcom Grange → Whatcom Farmers Co-op
intervals.who: Whatcom Farmers Co-op history; Whatcom News Apr 7 2015
intervals.note: Founded 1941 as Whatcom Grange; became Whatcom Farmers Cooperative in 1982. Members approved the CHS merger in April 2015.

intervals.label: CHS Northwest
intervals.note: CHS Northwest began operating Monday July 20 2015, after Whatcom Farmers Co-op merged into CHS, the national farmer-owned co-op.

intervals.label: North Cascade Meats organising
intervals.note: Farmers formed the North Cascade Meats collective in 2012; the Food Co-op's general manager and meat manager took part in the launch.

intervals.label: NABC co-op development help (USDA grant)
intervals.note: Technical assistance under a USDA Rural Cooperative Development Grant, including the securities exemptions that let the co-op sell shares. Year inferred from the launch; not published.

intervals.label: North Cascades Meat Producers Cooperative
intervals.note: Producer co-op established 2016. Cascade Cooperatives member.

intervals.label: North Cascade Meats beef sold at the Food Co-op
intervals.note: The Co-op's 'Welcome North Cascade Meats' post announced the beef; its date is not recorded here. Wide fuzz.

intervals.label: Puget Sound Food Hub, run by NABC
intervals.note: The food hub began under NABC's governance.

intervals.label: Puget Sound Food Hub Cooperative
intervals.who: WSU food hub case study; Cascade Cooperatives co-op map (2026)
intervals.note: Incorporated as a farmer-owned co-op in 2016, when governance passed from NABC to its own board. Outside Whatcom (Mount Vernon); serves Whatcom farms. Cascade Cooperatives member.

intervals.label: NW Cooperative Development Center
intervals.note: Founded by cooperatives in 1979; based in Olympia with Bellingham support staff.

intervals.label: Community to Community (C2C)
intervals.note: Founded 2003 by Rosalinda Guillén.

intervals.label: Farm Fund grant to C2C
intervals.note: Full title: Farm Fund grant: farmworker co-op development (C2C). Listed among the Farm Fund's earlier projects; year not given. Fuzz spans roughly 2004–2016.

intervals.label: NW Agriculture Business Center
intervals.note: Established 2006 in Mount Vernon (Skagit). USDA-funded rural co-op development centre.

intervals.label: Cascade Cooperatives network
intervals.note: Network of Whatcom and Skagit co-ops. Renamed from the Co-op Education Project in April 2019 (first as North Cascades Cooperatives); incorporated as a secondary co-op in January 2022; first board elected January 2023. 13 of the co-ops here are members; member-since dates are not published, so memberships are not drawn as links.

intervals.label: Co-op Education Project
intervals.note: Began in January 2014 as a group branching out from the Community Food Co-op Member Affairs Committee to teach the co-op model; ran How to Start a Co-op classes (2014) and On the Table events with WWU, NWCDC and the IDEA Institute (2015, 2017).
